haiku-low.q1: They see the generic message "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is stored and nothing is sent.
haiku-low.q2: Three or more reset_tokens rows exist in the last hour, so nothing more happens: no token and no email. The user sees the same generic message.
haiku-low.q3: A link works for 30 minutes after issue and only once. A newer link for the same account, or use of the link, ends it sooner.
haiku-low.q4: The link stays live. The user sees the reason on the form and may retry until the link expires.
haiku-low.q5: No devices stay logged in, because all sessions rows for the user are deleted, including the current one. The user is sent to the login page and must log in again.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. Nobody is notified, so the user is not told. They can request another link within the limit.
haiku-low.q7: The API builds the full link from the server-configured site URL plus the raw token, and puts it in the queued email job. The worker only sends it.
haiku-low.q8: It hashes the token from the link and looks up the row by that hash. The link is live only if used_at is empty and expires_at is in the future.
haiku-low.q9: It is counted from the user's reset_tokens rows with created_at in the last hour. Rows drop out of the count once they are more than an hour old.
haiku-low.q10: In the same transaction that inserts the new row, the account's unused older tokens are marked as used. This happens at issue time, before the email job is queued.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: save the new password hash, set used_at on the token, and delete all the user's sessions. The confirmation email is queued only after that commit.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic message "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is stored and nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: Nothing more happens: no token and no email. The user still sees the same generic message. (3 or more rows created in the last hour means do nothing.)
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes from issue, and it works once. It ends sooner if it is used, or if a newer link is issued for that account, which kills earlier unused links.
sonnet.q4: Still live. The form shows the rejection reason and the user can retry until the link expires.
sonnet.q5: None. All sessions rows for the user are deleted, including the current device. The user is redirected to the login page and logs in again with the new password; there is no automatic login.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job. Nobody is notified. The user can request another link, within the 3-per-hour limit.
sonnet.q7: The API generates the raw token and builds the finished link (site URL + raw token). It puts the recipient and finished link in the "send reset link" queue job after commit, and the worker only sends it. The raw token is never stored in the database.
sonnet.q8: It hashes the token from the link and finds the row by that hash. The link is good (live) if the row exists, used_at is empty and expires_at is in the future. Otherwise it shows the expired page.
sonnet.q9: It is not kept as a separate counter. It is a count of the user's reset_tokens rows with created_at in the last hour. Old requests drop out as their created_at passes the rolling one-hour window.
sonnet.q10: The user's unused older tokens are marked as used (used_at set). This happens in the same single transaction as inserting the new row, before the insert and before the queue job is added.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: save the new password hash in users, set used_at on the token, and delete all of the user's sessions rows. The "password changed" email is queued after the commit.
